source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 26: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Failure class: rank collective init hang. Treat it as a rendezvous/transport problem, not a model problem.

Assumptions: single job, static world size, PyTorch NCCL backend, no MIG partitioning changes mid-run.

Falsifiable hypothesis H26: the hang is caused by store rendezvous incompleteness (>=1 rank never reaches init_process_group), not by NCCL transport. If true, a rank-arrival barrier log will show a missing rank set and NCCL will never emit its channel-setup lines on any rank.

Controlled experiment: instrument every rank to log (hostname, LOCAL_RANK, RANK, WORLD_SIZE, MASTER_ADDR:PORT, monotonic timestamp) immediately before and after init_process_group with timeout=120s. Run the identical launch twice: (a) full world, (b) world reduced to 2 ranks on one node. If (b) succeeds and (a) shows a rank set that never printed the "before" line, the defect is in launcher/scheduler placement, not NCCL.

Measurements: per-rank pre/post init timestamps; NCCL_DEBUG=INFO channel/graph lines; `nvidia-smi -L` and CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES per rank; `ss -tanp` on MASTER_PORT; process state (D vs S) via /proc/<pid>/stack.

Confounders: a stale process from a prior run still holding MASTER_PORT; unequal container images across nodes producing different NCCL versions; ECC row-remap pending on one GPU making it enumerate late.

Evidence needed to accept H26: a rank whose "before init" log is absent while all others are present, with the launcher exit map confirming the process was never spawned or died pre-init.

Rollback threshold: if 2 controlled full-world reruns still hang after the placement fix, reject H26, escalate to transport-level bisection, and revert to the last known-good launcher revision. Do not leave hung ranks resident; they pin GPU memory and poison the next scheduling attempt.
risks: source_assistant is a rubric/checklist, not an answer; training on it teaches meta-description instead of diagnosis
leaving hung ranks resident pins GPU memory and corrupts the next scheduling attempt

source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 27: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Failure class: collective init hang. Variant focus: interface/transport selection.

Assumptions: rendezvous already proven healthy (all ranks reached init_process_group), so the stall is in NCCL bootstrap or transport setup.

Falsifiable hypothesis H27: NCCL auto-selected a non-routable interface (docker0/virbr0/an unconfigured second NIC), so the bootstrap TCP ring never closes. If true, forcing NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME to the known data-plane interface makes init complete deterministically.

Controlled experiment: A/B the same 2-node job with only one variable changed — NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME unset vs pinned to the verified interface. Keep image, world size, and node set identical. Three repeats each to rule out flakiness.

Measurements: `ip -o addr` on every node; NCCL_DEBUG=INFO + NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,NET to capture the chosen "NET/Socket : Using [ifname]" line per rank; per-rank init wall time; TCP connection table on the bootstrap port.

Confounders: NCCL may pick correctly and still hang because IB is half-configured — check whether NET/IB or NET/Socket was selected before blaming the ifname. Firewall rules that drop only cross-subnet traffic look identical to a bad ifname choice.

Evidence needed: log lines showing different ranks selecting different interfaces, or a selected interface with no route between node pairs (`ip route get <peer>` failing).

Rollback threshold: pinning the interface must fix it within 1 rerun. If it does not, revert the env change (do not accumulate untested NCCL env vars) and move to hypothesis H-topology. Never ship NCCL_P2P_DISABLE/NCCL_IB_DISABLE as a permanent "fix" without a recorded throughput regression measurement, because both silently degrade bandwidth.
risks: no guidance on which NCCL env vars are safe to keep; NCCL_IB_DISABLE/NCCL_P2P_DISABLE silently destroy bandwidth if left on
source answer omits the routing check, so an operator may pin a wrong interface
evidence_required: NCCL NET/Socket selection line per rank

source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 28: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Failure class: collective init hang. Variant focus: GPU visibility and device-to-rank mapping.

Assumptions: all ranks start, network is known good from a prior successful job on the same nodes today.

Falsifiable hypothesis H28: two ranks on the same node bound to the same physical GPU (duplicate local rank -> duplicate device ordinal), so NCCL's per-device communicator setup deadlocks waiting on a device that already has a communicator. If true, the device map will show fewer distinct UUIDs than ranks on that node.

Controlled experiment: have each rank log `torch.cuda.current_device()` plus the GPU UUID from pynvml, aggregate, and assert the UUID set size equals the node-local rank count. Then rerun with an explicit, launcher-provided LOCAL_RANK->device binding and compare.

Measurements: per-rank GPU UUID set; CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES as seen inside each container; `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,gpu_uuid`; NCCL init duration per rank.

Confounders: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES rewritten by both the scheduler and the training script (double remap) produces the same symptom; MIG instances change enumeration and make ordinals non-comparable across nodes.

Evidence needed: duplicate GPU UUIDs across distinct ranks, or a compute-apps table showing 2 PIDs from this job on one GPU while another GPU is idle.

Rollback threshold: if the UUID set is already 1:1 per node, H28 is refuted — stop tuning device binding and go to transport bisection. Any change to device-binding logic must be validated on a 1-node 2-GPU smoke run before touching the multi-node job, and reverted if step time regresses beyond 3%.
risks: duplicate device binding can silently corrupt a run rather than hang; source text gives no detection method
device-binding edits applied straight to a multi-node job without a single-node smoke run
evidence_required: per-rank GPU UUID set via pynvml

source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 29: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Failure class: collective init hang. Variant focus: minimal all-reduce bisection.

Assumptions: the real training job is too heavy to iterate on; we need a cheap reproducer.

Falsifiable hypothesis H29: the hang is reproducible by a bare all-reduce with no framework code, i.e. it is infrastructure-level, not a data-loader or checkpoint-load ordering bug. If true, a ~20-line torch.distributed script hangs at the same world size; if false, the hang is application-level (e.g. one rank blocked in dataset init before reaching the collective).

Controlled experiment: run the minimal all-reduce at world sizes 2, 4, 8, then across 2 nodes, same launcher and image. Record pass/fail per size. A clean scaling curve that breaks exactly when crossing the node boundary localizes the fault to inter-node transport; breaking at 8 within one node points to NVLink/P2P or device binding.

Measurements: per-configuration success/fail and init latency; NCCL_DEBUG=INFO ring/tree construction lines; `nvidia-smi topo -m` per node; host memory and pinned-memory limits (ulimit -l) which, if low, break IB registration.

Confounders: the minimal script may not import the same libraries, so a version-mismatch bug can hide; keep the same container and the same torch import path. Sporadic passes indicate a race — treat <3/3 success as failure.

Evidence needed: deterministic pass at N and deterministic hang at N+1 with only world size changed.

Rollback threshold: if the minimal script always passes across 3 repeats at full world size, refute H29 and instrument the training script itself (py-spy dump on every rank) instead of continuing infra changes. Do not modify production launcher config on the basis of a single non-reproducible hang.
risks: minimal reproducer may diverge from the real image and hide version bugs
single non-reproducible hang used to justify a production launcher change

source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 30: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Failure class: collective init hang. Variant focus: timeout semantics and silent straggler.

Assumptions: the job "hangs" as observed by the operator, but no NCCL timeout has fired yet.

Falsifiable hypothesis H30: this is not a true deadlock but an extreme straggler — one rank is doing slow work (cold page cache, checkpoint read from a throttled object store) before joining, and the configured timeout is large enough that it looks like a hang. If true, lowering the process-group timeout to 5 minutes converts the hang into a watchdog abort naming the exact laggard rank.

Controlled experiment: rerun with timeout=300s and TORCH_NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING enabled. Compare: does it complete at, say, 400s when the timeout is long, and abort with a rank identity when short? Record the join-time distribution across ranks over 3 runs.

Measurements: per-rank timestamp entering the first collective; storage read throughput on the slow node; watchdog abort messages with rank/collective sequence number; steady-state check that all ranks execute the same number of collectives (a mismatch means divergent control flow, a different bug).

Confounders: a genuinely deadlocked rank and a 10x-slow rank look identical for the first few minutes. Divergent control flow (rank-conditional branch skipping a collective) also presents as a hang and is NOT fixed by timeouts.

Evidence needed: a join-time histogram with one clear outlier that shrinks when the slow storage path is warmed or bypassed.

Rollback threshold: shortening the timeout is a diagnostic, not a fix — revert it before production, since aggressive timeouts turn recoverable slow epochs into job failures. If the outlier persists after storage warm-up, escalate to node-level hardware review rather than further timeout tuning.
risks: shortening the process-group timeout as a permanent setting turns slow epochs into job failures
divergent control flow misdiagnosed as a straggler
evidence_required: watchdog abort message with rank and collective seq
storage read throughput on the slow node

source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 31: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Failure class: collective init hang. Variant focus: single-node vs reduced-world comparison as the primary control.

Assumptions: we can schedule short exclusive runs on the suspect nodes.

Falsifiable hypothesis H31: the fault is bound to a specific node, not to world size. If true, holding world size constant while swapping which physical nodes participate will move the failure with one node.

Controlled experiment: fixed world size (e.g. 16 = 2 nodes x 8), rotate node membership across at least 4 candidate nodes so each node appears in some runs and is absent in others. Build a simple incidence table: failure should correlate with one node's presence with no counterexample.

Measurements: per-run node set and outcome; on the suspect node, `dmesg -T` for Xid/PCIe AER errors, `nvidia-smi -q` for ECC and retired/remapped pages, IB link state and rate via `ibstat` (expect all ports Active and at the nominal rate).

Confounders: a bad top-of-rack link makes a node *pair* fail, not a single node — design the rotation so at least one run pairs the suspect node with a different switch domain. Scheduler affinity may silently re-place you onto the same node.

Evidence needed: incidence table with zero failures when the suspect node is excluded across >=3 runs, plus a hardware-level signal (Xid, degraded link rate) on that node.

Rollback threshold: if the incidence table shows no single-node correlation after 6 runs, refute H31 and treat it as a fabric/config problem. Drain the suspect node from the scheduler only after a hardware signal is recorded; draining on suspicion alone costs capacity with no evidence.
risks: draining a node on suspicion with no hardware signal wastes capacity
scheduler affinity can silently re-place the job on the same suspect node, invalidating the rotation
evidence_required: dmesg -T Xid/PCIe AER on suspect node

source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 32: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Failure class: collective init hang. Variant focus: environment and version skew across nodes.

Assumptions: nodes are supposedly identical but were patched at different times.

Falsifiable hypothesis H32: NCCL/CUDA driver/container-image skew between nodes prevents transport negotiation, so bootstrap completes but transport setup stalls. If true, a per-node fingerprint diff will be non-empty and pinning all nodes to one image resolves it.

Controlled experiment: collect a fingerprint on every participating node (NCCL version from NCCL_DEBUG=VERSION, torch.version.cuda, driver version, image digest, ofed version) and diff. Then rerun restricted to nodes with an identical fingerprint. Only the fingerprint set changes between arms.

Measurements: fingerprint table; NCCL "Bootstrap : Using" and version banner per rank; init duration; whether NCCL_DEBUG output stops at the same subsystem on all ranks (transport) or at different points (rendezvous).

Confounders: identical NCCL versions can still differ in build flags (IB support compiled in or not); a matching image digest does not guarantee a matching host driver, and the driver is the usual skew source.

Evidence needed: a concrete version delta plus a homogeneous-node rerun that passes 3/3.

Rollback threshold: if homogeneous nodes still hang, refute H32 and stop image churn. Any fleet-wide driver or image roll must be staged (canary node set first) and reverted if the canary's init latency or step time regresses; never roll drivers under an active incident on all nodes at once.
risks: fleet-wide driver/image roll during an active incident
matching image digest wrongly assumed to imply matching host driver
evidence_required: per-node fingerprint table (NCCL, driver, CUDA, image digest, OFED)
canary node metrics before fleet roll

source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 33: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Failure class: collective init hang. Variant focus: RDMA/IB path specifically.

Assumptions: NCCL selected NET/IB, and the hang occurs after bootstrap.

Falsifiable hypothesis H33: RDMA queue-pair setup fails silently due to a GID/PKey or MTU mismatch (typical on RoCEv2 where GID index selection differs per node), so NCCL blocks in transport connect. If true, NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 will let the job start over TCP — slowly — which is a decisive diagnostic even though it is not the fix.

Controlled experiment: three arms on the same node pair: (a) as-is, (b) NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1, (c) as-is with NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX pinned to the RoCEv2 index verified via `show_gids`. Arm (b) succeeding while (a) hangs localizes the fault to RDMA; (c) succeeding confirms GID selection as the mechanism.

Measurements: `ibstat`/`ibv_devinfo` (port state, MTU, link layer), `show_gids` per node, PFC/ECN counters on the switch ports for RoCE, NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=NET output, `ib_write_bw` between the two nodes as a NCCL-independent bandwidth check.

Confounders: lossless-fabric misconfiguration (missing PFC) usually degrades throughput rather than hanging init — do not conclude PFC from a hang alone. Low `ulimit -l` breaks memory registration and mimics a fabric fault.

Evidence needed: ib_write_bw failing or far below line rate between the same pair, plus a GID/MTU delta.

Rollback threshold: NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 must never be left on — record the resulting bandwidth loss and revert it once the GID/MTU config is corrected. If arm (b) also hangs, RDMA is refuted as the cause; return to rendezvous-level analysis.
risks: NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 left enabled in production, causing a large unrecorded bandwidth regression
PFC/ECN misconfiguration inferred from a hang alone without counter evidence
evidence_required: ibstat / ibv_devinfo port state, MTU, link layer

source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 34: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Failure class: collective init hang. Variant focus: intra-node P2P / NVLink and topology.

Assumptions: single-node reproduction exists, so inter-node fabric is out of scope.

Falsifiable hypothesis H34: peer-to-peer access between two GPUs is unavailable or broken (IOMMU/ACS forcing traffic through the root complex, or an NVLink partition), so NCCL's intra-node transport setup blocks. If true, `nvidia-smi topo -m` will show an unexpected PHB/SYS path where NV# is expected, and a p2pBandwidthLatencyTest will fail or show near-zero P2P bandwidth for that pair.

Controlled experiment: run p2pBandwidthLatencyTest across all GPU pairs; then rerun the minimal all-reduce restricted to GPU subsets that exclude the suspect pair. Only the GPU subset changes.

Measurements: topo matrix; per-pair P2P bandwidth; `nvidia-smi nvlink -s` for link state and errors; IOMMU/ACS state from dmesg and kernel cmdline; NCCL_DEBUG=INFO lines showing which transport (P2P/SHM) each pair chose.

Confounders: on hosts where PCIe ACS is enabled, P2P is legitimately disabled and NCCL falls back to SHM — that is slow but should not hang, so a hang means something beyond ACS. A GPU already occupied by another tenant's process can also stall setup.

Evidence needed: a specific GPU pair with failed P2P plus an NCCL log stalling on exactly that pair.

Rollback threshold: if all pairs pass P2P at expected bandwidth, refute H34. Disabling ACS or changing IOMMU settings requires a host reboot and a documented rollback — do not apply it to a whole rack from a single-host observation; canary one host and revert if any workload regresses.
risks: ACS/IOMMU changes require reboot and were applied rack-wide from one host observation
a foreign tenant process on a GPU misread as a P2P fault
evidence_required: kernel cmdline / dmesg IOMMU and ACS state

source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 35: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Failure class: collective init hang. Variant focus: converting the ad-hoc hunt into a repeatable triage runbook.

Assumptions: hangs recur across weeks and multiple engineers; one-off fixes are not accumulating knowledge.

Falsifiable hypothesis H35: a fixed-order triage — (1) rank arrival, (2) device uniqueness, (3) interface selection, (4) minimal all-reduce scaling, (5) node rotation — classifies >=80% of these incidents within 15 minutes without changing production config. If true, replaying the runbook against the last N archived hang incidents reproduces the known root cause in most of them.

Controlled experiment: retrospective replay. Take archived incidents with confirmed root causes, run the runbook against their preserved logs blind to the recorded cause, and score classification accuracy. This is falsifiable: <80% means the runbook's ordering or checks are wrong.

Measurements: time-to-classification per incident; classification accuracy vs recorded root cause; how often a step was inconclusive; per-step yield so low-yield steps can be demoted.

Confounders: archived incidents are biased toward causes that were easy to find; incidents resolved by a reboot have no recorded mechanism and must be excluded rather than scored as successes.

Evidence needed: a scored replay table over >=10 incidents, plus one prospective incident classified correctly before the root cause is known.

Rollback threshold: if prospective accuracy falls below 60% over the next 5 incidents, revert to manual triage and re-derive the ordering from the new data. Automate collection (logs, topo, fingerprints) but never automate remediation actions such as node drain or env-var injection until the classifier's precision is measured on live incidents.
risks: retrospective incident set is biased toward easily-found causes
automating remediation (node drain, env injection) before classifier precision is measured on live incidents
evidence_required: scored retrospective replay table over >=10 incidents
prospective classification result on a live incident
